answer: Newcomers must be backed by strangers who stand to lose money. The wharf is a registry docking identities that share a funder, host or code fingerprint into one cluster. A pulse, one claimed identity, docks as the k-th of its cluster only when k sponsors outside that cluster each spend a horizon, the single lifetime sponsorship every member gets, bonded at 50 credits and slashed if the pulse is proven a clone. So 100 clones need 5,050 unrelated sponsors and 252,500 credits at risk. Sponsor rings evading clustering, or bribes above 50 credits, break it.
